answer: The ocean keeps no two drifters on the same path. Each ballot becomes a drifter dropped at a random point, riding one full tide — six hours, twelve minutes — drogue fifteen metres down, pinging hourly. Clone ballots die by the drift check: a farm's ballots, launched from one server, travel in one clump, and paths converging within 200 metres over one tide burn together, bond and all. A farm faking 10,000 ballots would need 10,000 drifters at $1,700 each — $17 million — plus a $25 bond each, $250,000 frozen. A meadow's bees scatter wide; farm ballots march in formation and drown.
